# Results — Study 642 (Turnaround Tuesday)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
**after a down Monday, the market bounces back on Tuesday** ("turnaround Tuesday"), the
mean-reversion cousin of the (mostly dead) Monday Effect. Offline & deterministic once
cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30**
(the last complete calendar month; the partial current month is dropped). Fingerprint
`bf55c945be2e` (SPY OHLC + adjusted close).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily SPY raw OHLC + adjusted (total-return) close (8,411 rows), 1993-01-29 → 2026-06-30 |
| Calendar | no hardcoded event table — "Monday"/"Tuesday" are calendar facts (`.dayofweek`) read straight off the trading-day index |
| Pairing | **1,567** Monday→Tuesday consecutive-session pairs (Tuesday sessions immediately preceded, in trading time, by a Monday session — a Monday market holiday breaks the adjacency and correctly drops that Tuesday from the sample) |
| Statistics | Welch *t* for the group splits (weekly, non-overlapping events); **Newey-West (5 lags)** *t* on the down-Monday-Tuesday dummy regression as the serial-correlation-robust cross-check; Wilson interval on the hit rate; 20-seed × 1,000-draw random-pair placebo |
| Execution / costs | one documented convention: enter SPY at the **Monday close** — the down-Monday flag is knowable at that exact instant, since it *is* that close, zero look-ahead — exit at the Tuesday close; one round trip = 2 × one-way cost × NAV; long-only, no borrow |
| Adjustment | **total-return** (adjusted close) throughout — this is a close-to-close calendar study, dividends are folded in, and every table below is on the same convention |

No survivorship on the Signal axis: SPY total return is a single continuous index
series, not a cross-sectional survivor panel.

## The headline — Tuesday return conditional on the prior Monday closing down

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| down-Monday Tuesday (n=684) | **+21.34 bps** |
| up-Monday Tuesday (n=883) | −2.21 bps |
| unconditional Tuesday (n=1,728) | +7.09 bps |
| all trading days (n=8,410) | +4.77 bps |
| Welch *t* vs unconditional Tuesday | **+2.38** |
| Welch *t* vs up-Monday Tuesday | **+3.85** |
| Welch *t* vs all days | **+3.04** |
| Newey-West *t* (dummy regression, 5 lags) vs all days | **+3.19** (coef +18.04 bps) |
| Newey-West *t* (dummy regression, 5 lags) vs Tuesdays only | **+3.80** (coef +23.60 bps) |
| hit rate (Tuesday positive) | **387/684 = 56.6%** (Wilson 95% [52.8%, 60.2%]) |

The conditional split clears the desk bar on **every** contrast: against the
unconditional Tuesday mean, against up-Monday Tuesdays, against all trading days, and
against the HAC cross-check. **Random-pair placebo:** observed +21.34 bps vs placebo
mean +8.05 bps (sd 3.27) over **20,000 draws (20 seeds × 1,000)** of a random subset of
684 Tuesdays → **p = 0.00005** — essentially no random label assignment produces it.

## Monday-specificity check — is this Monday, or generic reversal-after-any-down-day?

| pair | n | down-day mean | up-day mean | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Mon→Tue** | 1,567 | **+21.34 bps** | −2.21 bps | **+3.85** |
| Tue→Wed | 1,710 | +7.59 bps | +4.20 bps | +0.61 |
| Wed→Thu | 1,675 | +0.17 bps | +2.38 bps | −0.38 |
| Thu→Fri | 1,634 | +5.13 bps | +0.63 bps | +0.81 |
| Fri→Mon | 1,521 | +7.67 bps | +5.68 bps | +0.29 |
| pooled other four (excl. Mon→Tue) | 2,987 | +5.15 bps | +3.19 bps | **+0.66** |

Only **one** of the five weekday-pair reversals clears *t* = 2 — Monday→Tuesday. Pooled
together, the other four down-day → next-day reversals are statistically nothing
(*t* = +0.66). "Turnaround Tuesday" is not a repackaging of generic short-horizon
reversal; it is genuinely a **Monday**-specific pattern.

## Robustness — drop the two big crisis windows

Dropping the 2008-09 GFC (2008-09-01 → 2009-06-30) and 2020-03 COVID crash
(2020-02-15 → 2020-04-30) windows entirely:

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| down-Monday Tuesday, ex-crisis (n=652) | **+14.81 bps** |
| Welch *t* vs up-Monday Tuesday | **+3.14** |

The effect is not a handful of crisis-week outliers dragging the mean — it survives,
smaller but still significant, with the two loudest macro windows on the whole tape
removed.

## Era contrast — pre vs post 2000 (split 2000-01-01, named in the brief)

| era | down-Monday Tuesday | n | within-era Welch *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1993-01-29 → 2000-01-01 | +19.91 bps | 135 | +0.91 |
| 2000-01-01 → 2026-06-30 | +21.69 bps | 549 | **+2.20** |
| Welch *t* of the difference (late − early) | | | +0.15 |

No decay: the point estimate is essentially unchanged (+19.9 → +21.7 bps), and the
difference test finds nothing (*t* = +0.15). The 1990s slice alone can't certify the
effect on its own (only 135 events, *t* = +0.91 — a power problem, not a sign
reversal); the post-2000 slice, with four times the events, clears the bar on its own
(*t* = +2.20).

## The timer — buy the down Monday's close, sell the Tuesday close

Enter SPY at the Monday close (the flag is knowable at that instant — it *is* that
close, zero look-ahead), exit at the Tuesday close; one round trip = 2 × one-way cost ×
NAV; 684 events over 33.4 years ≈ 20.5 events/yr (≈ 8.1% of trading days).

| cost (one-way) | gross/event | net/event | ~ann. | one-sample *t* (net) | Sharpe (net) | worst single event |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5 bps | +21.3 bps | **+11.3 bps** | +2.32%/yr | **+2.14** | 0.37 | −4.58% |
| 10 bps | +21.3 bps | **+1.3 bps** | +0.27%/yr | **+0.25** | 0.04 | −4.68% |

At a typical **retail** one-way cost (5 bps) the net edge **barely** clears the
certification bar (*t* = 2.14) and Sharpe roughly halves from the gross 0.70 to 0.37.
At a realistic **institutional-but-not-trivial** cost (10 bps) the edge is
**statistically and economically dead** (*t* = 0.25, Sharpe 0.04, ann. +0.27%/yr) — one
extra basis point of friction per leg erases essentially the entire net return. The
position is only on ≈ 8% of trading days, so the total dollars at stake are thin, and a
single bad down-Monday-Tuesday (−4.6% to −4.7% net) can erase two to four years of net
edge at either cost level.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic i.i.d.-drift daily-return tape with a TUNABLE planted down-Monday →
Tuesday bounce; no network.

| world | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (bounce = 0), **20 seeds** | mean **−0.03** (sd 0.93), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 0/20 seeds** |
| planted bounce = +20 bps (seed 642) | **+4.70** |

The detector never fires on the null and lights up on a planted bounce. *(A
faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — REAL.** Down-Monday Tuesday **+21.34 bps** vs unconditional Tuesday
  +7.09 bps (Welch *t* = +2.38) and vs up-Monday Tuesday −2.21 bps (Welch *t* = +3.85);
  Newey-West *t* = +3.19/+3.80; random-pair placebo **p = 0.00005**; robust to dropping
  the GFC and COVID windows (*t* = +3.14); genuinely **Monday-specific**, not generic
  reversal wearing a costume (pooled other-weekday reversal *t* = +0.66); no decay
  across the pre/post-2000 split (diff *t* = +0.15). Clears **t ≥ 2** on the real tape
  several independent ways.
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** The net edge barely clears the bar at a retail 5 bps
  one-way cost (*t* = 2.14, Sharpe 0.37, +2.32%/yr) and is statistically dead at 10 bps
  (*t* = 0.25, Sharpe 0.04, +0.27%/yr). Only ≈ 8% time in market, and a single worst
  event (−4.6% to −4.7% net) erases years of the edge.
- **"Is this really about Monday, or just generic reversal?" — CONFIRMED (Monday).**
  Only the Mon→Tue pair clears *t* = 2 among all five weekday reversal pairs; the
  pooled other four are statistically nothing (*t* = +0.66). The folklore's specific
  claim — it's *Monday's* down day that matters — is the part that survives.
